topic: Red blood cell production: 2 million per second, no nucleus, 84% of cells, 120-day lifespan
hook: You make 2 million blood cells every second

slides.title: Built in your bones
slides.body: Marrow in your hips, ribs, spine and breastbone works nonstop: about 200 billion new red cells a day.
slides.image_prompt: Cross-section of a bone revealing glowing red spongy marrow, tiny red discs streaming out like sparks, dark background, scientific illustration style
slides.credit: Bruce Wetzel (photographer). Harry Schaefer (photographer) (Public domain) via wikimedia

slides.title: They delete their core
slides.body: As they mature, red blood cells push out their nucleus, leaving more room for oxygen-carrying hemoglobin.
slides.image_prompt: Close-up of smooth red biconcave discs floating in dark fluid, one disc ejecting a small dark sphere, soft cinematic lighting

slides.title: Most of you is blood
slides.body: Of your roughly 30 trillion cells, about 25 trillion are red blood cells.
slides.image_prompt: Huge crowd of red disc-shaped cells filling a vessel tunnel, a few rare different cells among them, deep red tones

slides.title: 120 days, then recycled
slides.body: Each one lives about four months. Your spleen and liver break it down and reuse its iron.
slides.image_prompt: Worn red disc dissolving into glittering iron particles that drift toward a fresh new red disc, dark red background, metaphor of recycling

cta: Part 2 tomorrow. Follow to catch it.
caption:
Right now your bone marrow is making about 2 million red blood cells every second. That adds up to around 200 billion a day, just to replace the ones wearing out.

Each cell lives about 120 days. Then your spleen and liver take it apart and reuse the iron for new ones. Follow for Part 2 tomorrow: the cells that defend you and the ones that stop you bleeding.

Did you know most of the cells in your body are red blood cells? 👇

Sources: Sender, Fuchs & Milo, PLoS Biology 2016; NCBI Bookshelf.
